newsitem.title: UK: British Energy July sales rise.
newsitem.headline: British Energy July sales rise.

text.p: British Energy Plc reported on Tuesday an increase to 5.58 terawatt hours (Twh) of output from its power stations sold to customers in July up from 4.35 Twh in July 1996.
TWh is a measure of the largest output of electrical power. The heat output of a one-bar electric fire is one kilowatt or one thousand watts.
The statutory outage at a reactor at Hinkley Point B in southern England started in July while the statutory outage continues on schedule at Torness in east Scotland.
One reactor at Heysham 2 in northwest England returned from statutory outage on July 15.
The other Hinkley Point B reactor was shut down on July 29 for repairs but is expected to be back in service within the next week, the company said in a statement.
